oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A Two-Stage Spatiotemporal Fusion Framework for Land Surface Temperature With Environmental Variable Correction
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Land surface temperature (LST) is a key parameter in Earth system science, yet a tradeoff between spatial and temporal resolution limits the quality of satellite products. Spatiotemporal fusion offers a viable solution, but existing methods often suffer from limited feature utilization and insufficient correction by environmental variables. To address these challenges, we propose a novel two-stage spatiotemporal fusion framework (TSFF). The framework first employs the bidirectional multifeature spatiotemporal fusion network with generative adversarial network to generate an initial high-resolution LST estimate. This network leverages a bidirectional structure to enhance temporal constraints and a multiscale attention mechanism to capture complex spatial dependencies. Subsequently, a land surface temperature correction network (LST-CorrNet) refines this estimate by performing a residual correction aided by environmental variables. LST-CorrNet incorporates heterogeneous auxiliary data—digital elevation model, total column water vapor, and longwave radiation—to account for thermodynamic influences from topography, the atmosphere, and surface radiative processes. TSFF performance was evaluated through testing using the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis v.5 (ERA5)-Land and Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) LST products. The final hourly, MODIS-resolution LST products show excellent agreement with ground-truth data across diverse land cover types (mean absolute error: 2.29–3.50 K; root-mean-square error: 3.20–4.75 K; correlation coefficient: 0.96–0.98). The fused LST not only preserves fine spatial details but also accurately captures temporal dynamics. This study highlights the significant benefits of a two-stage approach that uses explicit environmental variables to correct and enhance deep learning-based spatiotemporal fusion models.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: An Improved Coregistration Strategy Integrating Local Iterative Pixel Offset Tracking and Weighted ESD for Sentinel-1 TOPS Mode DInSAR Measurement in Nonstationary Scenarios
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The Sentinel-1 (S1) satellites, operating at C-band in terrain observation by progressive scans (TOPS) mode, provide unprecedented opportunities for measuring large-scale tectonic motions using interferometric synthetic aperture radar. However, the azimuth-varying Doppler centroid imposes stringent coregistration requirements, for which the enhanced spectral diversity (ESD) method is typically employed to achieve the required high-precision azimuth coregistration. In practical applications, however, the ESD method is inevitably affected by various disturbances, especially by pronounced large-scale and nonstationary azimuth deformation. Such disturbances not only degrade the coregistration accuracy of the ESD method but also cause phase jumps at burst edges, thereby complicating the subsequent phase unwrapping. To address these issues, this study proposes an improved coregistration strategy that integrates the local iterative pixel offset tracking and weighted ESD to mitigate the effects of azimuth deformation and enhance the robustness of the ESD method. Furthermore, the coherence gradient consistency indicator is introduced to embed the proposed method into the standard processing workflow, enabling automated selection of appropriate coregistration strategies. The effectiveness of the proposed method was validated using S1 TOPS repeat-pass data acquired over four representative regions. By applying the proposed method, the phase jumps observed in the conventional processing were effectively corrected, demonstrating its superior accuracy and stability in complex deformation scenarios.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Vegetation Water Content Estimation Using Optical and Microwave Remote Sensing
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Accurate estimation of vegetation water content (VWC) is crucial for understanding terrestrial ecosystem dynamics. However, conventional remote sensing retrieval methods struggle to capture the complex, nonlinear relationships between VWC and variables, such as vegetation optical depth (VOD), leaf area index (LAI), and vegetation height (VH), across diverse land cover types. While machine learning provides potential solutions, models with fixed architectures often exhibit poor generalization. This study introduced a novel framework for VWC estimation using a conditional adaptive neural network (CANN), which dynamically tailored its network parameters to input data characteristics. The model predicted VWC using VOD, LAI, VH, and the International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme land cover type as inputs. Results show that the proposed VWC estimates in this study were highly consistent with the reference VWC, by achieving a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.94 [root-mean-square error (RMSE) = 1.13 kg/m<sup>2</sup>] against LFMC-VWC (VWC derived by Globe-Live Fuel Moisture Content) and an R of 0.95 (RMSE = 2.48 kg/m<sup>2</sup>) against normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI)-VWC (VWC derived by NDVI). In addition, the temporal dynamics of CANN-VWC closely followed the SMAPVEX in situ VWC measurements, exhibiting more competitive performance than the NDVI-VWC estimates.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A Physics-Guided Multibranch Adaptive Multilevel Attention Fusion Network for Sea Oil-Spill Detection in Sentinel-1 SAR Imagery
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has been widely used for oil-spill monitoring because of its all-weather and all-day imaging capability. However, simple concatenation of multiple oil-spill features extracted from SAR images, such as polarization, intensity, texture, and wind speed, often introduces semantic interference and degrades detection performance. Moreover, these existing oil-spill detection methods still have a limited ability to deal with the small-scale and fragmented oil spills under complex sea backgrounds and class imbalance. To address these issues, this article proposes a physics-guided multibranch adaptive multilevel attention fusion network (MAMAF-Net) based on Swin Transformer and a deep convolutional neural network. The network includes four independent branches to handle the features with different physical meanings, enabling feature decoupling and adaptive fusion. In addition, several specialized modules, such as the edge enhancement module, multilevel attention fusion module, hybrid Focal–Tversky loss, and the entropy-weighted hysteresis enhancement, are incorporated into the network to enhance the feature representation of oil spills during the encoding stage and the precise reconstruction of oil-spill areas during the decoding stage. Comparative experiments conducted on a self-constructed SAR oil-spill dataset demonstrate that the proposed model achieves more complete region extraction and more accurate boundary localization under complex sea conditions, outperforming several mainstream deep-learning networks with the highest mean mIoU of 92.11% and BF1 of 83.56%. Ablation experiments of the modules and branches verify the effectiveness of individual components and the multibranch collaborative mechanism for oil-spill detection, indicating that the proposed model achieves improved overall performance and enhanced robustness under complex sea conditions. Overall, the proposed MAMAF-Net has strong performance in feature decoupling, boundary recognition, and noise robustness, offering an efficient and reliable solution for marine oil-spill detection.
